subject: math

objective.text: Read tens and ones, use ten-plus facts with other tens, and find the next ten within 100.

source_ref.section: L2 lesson content in the combined Module 1 concept JSON; objective adapted from its explanations and questions

explanations.title: L2 Value of tens and ones
explanations.text: A quick ten is a stick of 10. Count the tens first. Then count the ones. 2 tens and 2 ones make 22. 20 plus 2 equals 22.

source_ref.section: L2 Fluency: The Value of Tens and Ones

explanations.title: L2 Make the next ten
explanations.text: 8 needs 2 to make the next ten. 28 needs 2 to make 30. 58 needs 2 to make 60. The ones tell you how many.

source_ref.section: L2 Fluency: Make the Next Ten (8, 28, 58: S: 2)

explanations.title: L2 A ten fact helps with other tens
explanations.text: Knowing 10 plus 3 helps with 50 plus 3. Both add 3 ones. 10 plus 3 equals 13. So 50 plus 3 equals 53.

source_ref.section: L2 Student Debrief (how does knowing 10 + 3 help us with 50 + 3)

assets_required.why_this_method: Needs an exact number of tens sticks and ones dots. Image models cannot count.
assets_required.description: A quick-ten picture: each ten is a stick of 10 dots, each one is a single dot. For make-a-ten problems the extra dots can be drawn as circles and Xs.
must_show_exactly: T sticks of 10 dots and U single dots represent 10T + U for the current lesson stimulus.
For make-a-ten tasks, the added dots complete the next ten first and the remaining dots stay outside that group.
states_or_frames: configured from the current lesson question stimulus
assets_required.interaction: Shows the picture. The child answers by typing or speaking. Adding tens or Xs can be animated one at a time.
assets_required.alt_text: Sticks of ten dots and some single dots showing a two-digit number.
assets_required.generation_caption: Flat quick-ten drawing: T vertical sticks of 10 dots and U single dots, plain background, no text. [Build by code]

Build the 1 lesson visual specifications by code and check exact quantities against each rubric.
Lesson 2 was extracted by lesson-specific IDs. Its objective and scoped asset states are adapted. Review them against the original lesson before use.

The source is 8 markdown files with no printed page numbers, no images and no 'This file derived from' footer. Every page is 'n/a' with a section name. source_version is 'not_stated_in_file' and source_refs holds one item for the whole zip. Fill both in from the original PDFs.

The worksheets have no printed titles in these files. They were named by order after the Exit Ticket instructions: Lessons 1 to 3 start with Sprint A and Sprint B. Lessons 3 to 8 then show Problem Set, Exit Ticket, Homework. Lessons 1 and 2 show Exit Ticket, Homework. A person must confirm this against the PDFs. Section names that say Problem Set, Exit Ticket or Homework depend on it.
The source is a teacher script for a class with a Rekenrek, cards and partners. All child text was rewritten for a screen. Needs age-appropriate wording review.

ext_g1_add_subtract_within_10, ext_k_say_ten_counting and ext_g1_place_value_tens_ones are external prerequisite cards that do not exist yet. The source names Grade 1 and Kindergarten work as earlier learning but does not teach it.

The source prints no answers for Sprints, Exit Tickets, Homework or Problem Sets, and none for most Fluency and word-problem items. Every such key is derived. Each was solved by code from the printed item, then checked against the lesson text.

visual_generation_rules: Diffusion cannot count reliably. Any picture where an exact number of objects matters must be built by code (SVG or widget) or drawn by an artist.
Diffusion is allowed only for: style or background art, and single icons (one ball, one pencil, one leaf, one character) that code then tiles to the exact count.
Every visual must be checked by a person: the count shown must equal the stimulus in the question and the rubric answer key.
Animations are described as frames with exact counts per frame, so they can be built or generated and then checked frame by frame.
Visual explanations are valid only when the asset exists (pipeline doc, Planner rules).
